outliers: google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview: scored 9 vs median 7 - Gemini saw the direct ownership ('I shouldn't make you jump through more hoops') as fully empathetic, while other judges found the empathy reactive and transactional

openai/gpt-6.1-sol: scored 5 vs median 9 - OpenAI penalized unverified operational promises (same-day refund, credit preventing billing) and the unretracted earlier guarantee; other judges praised the honesty about timelines and limits
anthropic judge (claude-opus-5-5): scored 6 vs median 9 - focused on the early overpromise about the account credit protecting the external bill and ungrounded timelines

assessment: The agent stumbled initially by requesting redundant verification despite the customer offering transaction IDs, and overpromised that an account credit would protect the external bill—later walked back. However, it recovered well with concrete pending-vs-posted resolution paths, a refund reference number, a useful bank provisional-credit suggestion, and honest timelines without invented guarantees. Empathy was competent but reactive, engaging with the customer's urgency only after pushback rather than from the start. No rule or tool errors were confirmed across judges.
judge_agreement: Judges unanimously agreed the first turn was a misstep (over-asking, overpromising) and that turns 2-3 showed strong recovery with concrete, honest guidance; none found rule errors. The main disagreement was severity of the early overpromise: Gemini, DeepSeek, and Qwen viewed the later corrections as largely redeeming (scores 8-10), while OpenAI and Anthropic treated the misleading initial assurance and unverified promises as significant ongoing deductions (scores 5-6), particularly for policy clarity.
